nodes.title: Material Breach and Constructive Conditions
nodes.conceptSummary:
When one party commits a material breach, the non-breaching party's constructive duties under the contract are suspended.
The core invariant is substantial performance: if a breach is minor and immaterial, the non-breaching party must still perform their obligations and may only sue for damages, rather than terminating the contract.

nodes.title: Expectation Damages and Mitigation
nodes.conceptSummary:
Remedies for breach aim to place the aggrieved party in the position they would have occupied had the contract been fully performed.
The fundamental invariant is the duty to mitigate: an injured party cannot recover damages for losses that could reasonably have been avoided without undue risk, burden, or humiliation.

conceptualVariants.content: The fundamental invariant is the duty to mitigate: an injured party cannot recover damages for losses that could reasonably have been avoided without undue risk, burden, or humiliation.

proceduralPerturbations.expectedBoundaryBehavior: "Recovery is reduced by the avoidable salary under the doctrine of avoidable consequences: an aggrieved party has an affirmative duty to mitigate damages with reasonable effort."
